newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia July palm oil output seen up 5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia July palm oil output seen up 5.0 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in July is expected to increase by five percent or about 40,000 tonnes over June, private crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Monday.
Production is June was 787,807 tonnes, offcial Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) figures showed.
Wong forecast palm oil stocks at the end of July at 865,000-875,000 tonnes, compared with PORLA's 786,123 at end-June.
Exports in July were projected at 630,000-635,000 tonnes against PORLA's 612,124 in June.
Wong said in a report that field crop surveys conducted last week indicated production growth would continue, albeit, at a slower pace.

"The seasonal rise in production would comfortably exceed increases in exports and result in a big build-up in stocks," he said, adding that his projection of crude palm oil production this year is revised upward to 8.9 million tonnes.
Wong said palm oil stocks at the end of September were expected "to be well above the one-million tonne level, possibly to 1.06 million tonnes."
Malaysia palm oil supply-demand estimate/projection as of July 21, 1997. (All figures in '000 tonnes)
